description:
Bind a FLOAT, BOOLEAN, or STRING variable to a node property. COLOR variables go through set_fill / set_stroke / jsx instead — see Skip when.

`prop` is a registry-backed non-color field. Its schema is the complete accepted vocabulary, including aliases such as gap → itemSpacing, padding → paddingTop, corner → cornerRadius, and font-size → fontSize.

`variable` accepts an exact ID or a collection-qualified selector such as `{collection: "Layout Tokens", name: "Spacing/CardGap"}`. Use the selector when the exact collection and variable names are known: copy both fields exactly from the request and do not drop qualifiers or suffixes. Never synthesize a variable ID from a collection name, variable name, or namespace; use `list_variables` when the qualified name is unknown or ambiguous.

Use when:
- Wiring a numeric token (spacing, radius, fontSize) to a node so it tracks the design system
- Toggling a BOOLEAN visibility via a global variable
- Binding STRING content (e.g. characters) to a localized text variable

Returns: { data: { message, nodeId, variableId } } on success.

May carry warnings:
  MODE_FALLBACK — variable lacks a value for one of the node's reachable modes; Figma falls back to default mode along the mode chain.

Inline errors (LLM can self-correct from these):
  MISSING_MODE_VALUES — variable missing required modes. Response `data.recommended_next_action` carries a ready-to-call create_variable with the missing modes populated.

Skip when:
- Variable is COLOR — use set_fill({node, bg: "$VarName"}), set_stroke({node, color: "$VarName"}), or specify fill/bg="$VarName" at jsx creation
- Target prop is a Paint (fills, strokes) — same as COLOR above
- Variable missing required modes — call create_variable first to fill them, or expect MISSING_MODE_VALUES

Mode selection tip: when the node is a Tablet/Mobile variant (name or variant property contains "Tablet"/"Mobile"), match its property value against the Tablet/Mobile mode column from list_variables — not Desktop.

Examples:
```text
bind_variable({node: "1:2", prop: "fontSize", variable: "VariableID:1:6"})
bind_variable({node: "1:3", prop: "itemSpacing", variable: {collection: "Layout Tokens", name: "Spacing/CardGap"}})
bind_variable({node: "1:4", prop: "visible", variable: "VariableID:1:8"})
bind_variable({node: "1:5", prop: "characters", variable: "VariableID:1:9"})
```

Binding rules:
- A `characters` binding and literal text cannot coexist. Binding `characters` makes text update with the active mode; a later `set_text` call removes that binding. Change variable-driven copy with `set_variable_value`.
- For a Tablet or Mobile variant, compare the node value with the corresponding mode column rather than Desktop. If the relative difference is 20% or more, confirm the match before binding.
- A bound property reads from its variable. Changing the variable changes every consumer. To correct one node without affecting other consumers, bind that node to a different variable.
- Before a batch bind, show the planned node-to-variable mapping and each value difference. Inspect the nodes afterward because binding replaces their previous literal values.
- To switch a node/page to a mode (Dark, Mobile, CN), use set_variable_mode — modes are set on the consumer node, not the variable.

prop.description: Registry-backed non-color node field that should resolve from the variable.

name.description: Exact variable name/path within that collection

variable.description: Exact VariableID, or an exact collection-qualified selector

name: bind_variable
